blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Lesson 12.4.2's job_outcomes.py runs the medium portfolio and the large portfolio, each with a 1-second limit. How did the two jobs end?

options.text: large: no plan; medium: a plan short of its proof, with a gap
options.says: Right: large printed time_limit, plan: no; medium printed time_limit with a plan and its gap.

options.text: large: no plan; medium: a proven optimal plan with a gap of 0
options.says: Medium printed time_limit with a gap; it was not proven in 1 s.

options.text: large: a plan short of its proof; medium: a plan short of proof
options.says: Large printed plan: no; only medium found a plan in the second.

options.text: large: a plan short of its proof; medium: a proven optimal plan
options.says: Large printed time_limit with plan: no, and medium printed time_limit with a plan.

origin.section: Every Way a Solve Ends Has Its Own Status

questions.stem: Lesson 12.4.2's background_tasks.py posts one job through TestClient, then polls it once. Its stand-in solve sleeps for a fixed time. What did it print?

options.text: 202 queued after 3 s; first poll: optimal
options.says: The printed post line ends 'after 1 s': the stand-in solve sleeps 1 second.

options.text: 202 queued after 1 s; first poll: optimal
options.says: Right: POST /jobs -> 202 {'job_id': 'job-1', 'status': 'queued'} after 1 s, then optimal.

options.text: 202 queued after 5 s; first poll: optimal
options.says: The printed post line ends 'after 1 s', not 5 s: time.sleep(1) is the solve.

options.text: 202 queued after 2 s; first poll: optimal
options.says: The printed post line ends 'after 1 s', not 2 s: time.sleep(1) is the solve.

origin.section: BackgroundTasks Runs After the Response, and Keeps No Status

questions.stem: In lesson 12.4.2's job_outcomes.py, the fifth job asks HiGHS for 2 threads; the four jobs before it set no thread count, and a sixth job follows. How did the fifth and sixth jobs end?

options.text: fifth: optimal on 2 threads; sixth: optimal on the default count
options.says: The fifth printed failed with HighsStatus: kError [INTERNAL].

options.text: fifth: failed, kError [INTERNAL]; sixth: failed the same way
options.says: The sixth job, with no thread setting, printed optimal.

options.text: fifth: optimal on the default count; sixth: optimal as well
options.says: The setting was not ignored: the fifth printed failed.

options.text: fifth: failed, kError [INTERNAL]; sixth: optimal as before
options.says: Right: the first HiGHS solve fixed the process's thread count (lesson 4.2.4); the next job ran normally.
